title: Jesus Shows Us True Humility
reading:
Before Jesus went to the cross, He prayed to His Father and said, "Not my will, but Yours be done."

Jesus trusted His Father completely. Even when the path was hard, He chose obedience.

Andrew Murray wrote that humility is the heart of Jesus. Jesus did not come to do His own will — He came to follow His Father's will in everything.

When we choose to trust and obey God, we are walking the same path Jesus walked.

Humility means saying, "God, I trust You more than my own way."
reflection: Why do you think Jesus trusted His Father even when it was difficult? Is there something in your life where you want your own way instead of God's way? What might it look like to pray, "Not my will, but Yours"?
abide: When we trust God's will above our own, we begin to grow in the same humility Jesus showed.
murrayReading:
What is the incarnation but His heavenly humility, His emptying Himself and becoming man? What is His life on earth but humility; His taking the form of a servant?

In heaven, where He was with the Father, in His birth, in His life, in His death, in His sitting on the throne, it is all, it is nothing but humility.

Christ is the humility of God embodied in human nature; the Eternal Love humbling itself, clothing itself in the garb of meekness and gentleness, to win and serve and save us.

If humility be the first, the all-including grace of the life of Jesus, then the health and strength of our spiritual life will entirely depend upon our putting this grace first too.
